title: stable-routing-rule-dsl: add strict schema validation and safe migration path
creator: Amelia Chen
description: Background: The current smart routing rules are a loosely validated YAML/JSON mixture we parse at runtime. This causes silent mis-routings, unclear error messages in Console, and brittle rollouts when teams author region/tier/fallback rules. Objective: Refactor the policy engine to (1) introduce a formal DSL schema for routing rules, (2) add compile-time/CI validation and user-friendly validation errors, and (3) ship a backward-compatible migration tool that converts legacy policy configs to the new schema with warnings and automatic fixes where safe. Scope: region selection (geo-based policies), tier routing (hosted/dedicated/private tiers), and fallback model variants (compatible model mapping and fallthrough semantics). Non-goals: changing routing semantics beyond documented fallbacks or altering runtime fallback ordering except to make it explicit in schema. Approach: 1) Define a JSON Schema and a compact DSL AST for the routing rules that explicitly models predicates, match priorities, target tiers, region constraints, and fallback chains. 2) Implement a schema validator library in Go (shared runtime) and a TypeScript/Node validator for Console/CI. 3) Add lint rules and validation hooks in the Console policy editor and infra CI so misconfigured rules fail fast. 4) Build an automated migration tool (dry-run + apply) which: a) detects common legacy idioms, b) emits warnings for ambiguous configs, and c) offers suggested transformations. 5) Add integration tests + canary rollout with feature flag to evaluate production behavior for a subset of customers. Key design decisions and trade-offs: - Strict schema vs. flexibility: we aim for an expressive but opinionated schema; extension points (custom predicates) will be gated behind explicit versioning. - Validation location: both client-side (Console/CLI) and server-side validation to avoid bad configs reaching the runtime. - Migration strategy: favor non-destructive suggestions; automatic conversion only when semantics are preserved. Acceptance criteria: - All routing configs accepted by runtime pass the new validator or provide actionable error messages. - Migration tool correctly translates >90% of existing configs in sample corpus without semantic changes. - Console policy editor surfaces schema errors inline and prevents save when there are critical issues. - No increase in 95th percentile policy evaluation latency by more than 5% in a canary test. - Feature flagged rollout and monitoring dashboards for config validation failures, migration adoption, and routing mismatches. Migration plan: 1) Collect sample corpus from customers and internal configs (ENG-4899). 2) Iterate on schema in an RFC with PM and Design. 3) Implement validators + migration tool in a feature branch. 4) Add Console integration and CI gating. 5) Canary rollout to <5% of production requests for 48h. 6) Gradual ramp with telemetry checks and rollback triggers. Testing & observability: - Unit tests for parser/validator and AST transforms. - Integration tests that compile policies and run evaluation against synthetic traffic (region/tier combinations). - End-to-end tests that exercise fallback chains and ensure correct logging. - Telemetry: validation failures per hour, migrated-config success rate, routing mismatches (simulated vs. active policy). Risks and mitigations: - Risk: migration changes behavior for edge policies. Mitigation: conservative dry-run mode and manual approvals for auto-apply. - Risk: schema too restrictive for advanced customers. Mitigation: schema versioning and opt-in extensibility flags. - Risk: validator performance regression. Mitigation: implement and benchmark both Go and Node validators; add caching of compiled policies. Rollout notes: - Feature flag route: policy-schema-v2. - Start with internal tenants and opt-in customers, coordinate with Solutions and Customer Success. - Communicate breaking changes and provide rollback instructions and support window. Deliverables: - JSON Schema spec doc + short DSL reference. - Go validator and runtime-safe compiled policy representation. - TypeScript validator for Console/CLI. - Migration tool (dry-run/apply) with a confluence doc and sample outputs. - Console inline validation and helpful error UX. - Test suite and dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: JSON Schema and DSL reference published in Docs with examples for region/tier/fallback
Server-side validator rejects invalid rules with clear error codes
Console shows inline validation and prevents saving critical-invalid rules
Migration tool dry-run translates >=90% of sampled legacy configs without semantic change
Canary metrics show <=5% increase in 95p policy eval latency and no unexplained routing mismatches
